patches.old: 1. **Combinatorial V(D)J joining**: 40 V × 25 D × 6 J = ~6,000 possible heavy chain combinations; ~200 possible light chain combinations. Together: ~1.2 × 10⁶ combinations from gene segment choice alone.
patches.new: 1. **Combinatorial V(D)J joining**: 40 V × 25 D × 6 J = ~6,000 possible heavy chain combinations; ~200 κ (40 V × 5 J) plus ~120 λ (30 V × 4 J) light chain combinations, or ~320 in all.
patches.reason: The light-chain count left out λ, and the heavy × light product was double-counted here and again under pairing (point 3).

patches.old: With ~6,000 heavy chain and ~200 light chain possibilities, this gives ~1.2 × 10⁶ combinations
patches.new: With ~6,000 heavy chain and ~320 light chain possibilities, this gives ~2 × 10⁶ combinations

patches.old: - **IL-4**: promotes switching to IgG1 and IgE
patches.new: - **IL-4** (with IL-13): promotes switching to IgE, and to IgG1 in mice (IgG4 in humans)
patches.reason: IL-4 drives IgE plus IgG1 in mice but IgE plus IgG4 in humans.

patches.old: IgM is particularly efficient because its pentameric structure can engage C1q (the first complement component) with both arms of C1q simultaneously.
patches.new: IgM is particularly efficient because a single antigen-bound pentamer can engage several of C1q's six globular heads at once, whereas IgG needs several molecules bound close together.
patches.reason: C1q has six globular heads, not two arms; activation needs multiple heads bound.

visual.title: V(D)J recombination
visual.alt: Four rows of DNA. Germline: about 40 functional V, about 25 D and 6 J segments followed by constant genes. RAG1/RAG2 first join one D to one J, deleting the DNA between them, then join one V to the DJ; TdT adds N-nucleotides at the junctions, which form the highly variable CDR3. The VDJ exon is transcribed with C-mu (and C-delta by alternative splicing) to make IgM and IgD. A side box counts diversity: about 6,000 heavy-chain combinations, about 200 kappa and 120 lambda light-chain combinations, about 2 million pairings, with junctional diversity and somatic hypermutation adding much more. A footer contrasts RAG (V(D)J joining before antigen; loss causes SCID) with AID (class switching and hypermutation after antigen).
visual.caption: Segment counts are approximate; constant genes are shown in simplified order.
